why_cnn_preferred_for_demo: CORRECTED after actually measuring both (realtime_replay_demo.py, single-window CPU inference): RF's per-window latency was mean=214.9ms, p95=244.5ms, max=677.3ms - the max BREAKS the 500ms hop budget. CNN measured mean=18.8ms, p95=31.6ms, max=148.5ms - comfortably under budget. This is the opposite of an earlier, unverified guess in this same file that preferred RF for 'no PyTorch dependency' reasons without having measured RF's actual single-sample latency yet - that guess was wrong: RF's RandomForestClassifier(n_jobs=-1) most likely pays multiprocess dispatch overhead on every single-window predict_proba() call, overhead that a bigger batch would amortize but a live one-window-at-a-time stream cannot. SUPERSEDED by why_ensemble_preferred_for_demo below: that overhead hypothesis was confirmed this session (n_jobs=1 profiling) and turned the RF latency problem into a non-problem, unblocking the ensemble now deployed as the live default. Kept verbatim for history. The poster AUC should still cite whichever single model actually scores higher on test.npz - this field is about live-demo latency safety only.
why_ensemble_preferred_for_demo: Miss-rate investigation (scripts/ensemble_investigation.py, data/processed/ml/ensemble_investigation_summary.json), separate from and complementary to the earlier false-alarm work: averaging RF+CNN's fog_score probabilities (both already-trained, unchanged) raised PD_only val AUC from 0.7996 (RF)/0.8163 (CNN) to 0.8343 - a genuine, threshold-INDEPENDENT ranking improvement, not a threshold-tuning artifact. At a threshold picked to match-or-beat the deployed CNN's own PD_only val FPR_stop (0.4507, so this does not undo the separate false-alarm-rate work), the ensemble's threshold=0.39: val FPR_stop 0.4468 (slightly better), val sensitivity 0.805 (small +0.44pp gain per-window) but caught 2 ADDITIONAL real val FoG episodes at the window-level state-machine granularity that actually matters for this project (37/45 -> 39/45, i.e. missed 8 -> missed 6, a 25% relative reduction in real freezes the state machine never reaches Active for) - confirmed generalizing on held-out test.npz, where sensitivity rose 0.8408->0.8753 AND FPR_stop IMPROVED 0.3464->0.3178 simultaneously (no false-alarm cost at all on test). RF-alone was tempting on raw episode-catch count (42/45) but explicitly rejected: its own FPR_stop (0.6228) is far worse than CNN's, i.e. that number is bought with a big false-alarm regression this task must not reintroduce. Latency was the one real risk (running RF on every window) - resolved by profiling RF with n_jobs=1 (not previously tried live): mean~16ms/p95~22ms/max~32ms per window, vs n_jobs=-1's mean~39ms/max~150ms+ on the same single-window call pattern - combined ensemble worst case (RF n_jobs=1 + CNN) measured ~85ms, comfortably inside the 500ms hop budget. live_detector.py's LiveFogDetector now supports model_name='ensemble' (loads both models, RF forced to n_jobs=1, averages fog_score) alongside the existing 'rf'/'cnn' single-model modes, which remain available unchanged. NOTE: this paragraph documents the ORIGINAL (non-tremor-augmented) ensemble decision and is kept verbatim for history/lineage of the AUC/latency reasoning, which is still architecturally valid - see why_tremor_augmented_aug_small_deployed below for what changed the actual deployed WEIGHTS and THRESHOLDS after this.
why_tremor_augmented_aug_small_deployed: Deployed weights/thresholds changed on 2026-09-01 from the original (non-augmented) RF/CNN to the 'aug_small' condition of scripts/standing_freeze_tremor_augmentation_train.py, after a dedicated threshold search (scripts/standing_freeze_tremor_augmentation_threshold_search.py, data/processed/ml/standing_freeze_tremor_augmentation_threshold_search_summary.json) found an operating point that captures the augmentation's real AUC gain WITHOUT the episode-level regression that naive Youden's J picked. BACKGROUND: standing_freeze_tremor_injection_investigation.py found the (then-)deployed models recognized a synthetic 'real Stand window + injected real Walk/Turn-context tremor waveform' as FoG only 13-22% of the time (vs 88-96% for the identical tremor waveform left in its original Walk/Turn context) - the training set had zero labeled-positive examples of 'freeze-band oscillation with near-zero everything else'. standing_freeze_tremor_augmentation_train.py fixed this by adding synthetic Stand+tremor windows (TRAIN-split sourced only, real val/test never touched) as EXTRA FoG-labeled training examples at two doses (aug_small=+500, aug_large=+2000, on top of the unchanged ~57k-window real train set) and retraining RF+CNN with the exact train_final_model.py recipe. Both doses genuinely improved PD_only AUC (ensemble val 0.8343->aug_small 0.8543/aug_large 0.8433; test 0.9123->0.9167/0.9104) and dramatically improved synthetic Stand+tremor recognition, but AT EACH CONDITION'S OWN YOUDEN'S-J THRESHOLD, episode-level (state-machine) detection on real val FoG episodes REGRESSED (ensemble 39/45 -> aug_small 36/45 / aug_large 40/45) - because Youden's J on the reshaped augmented score distribution picked a substantially higher/more conservative threshold (e.g. CNN's own Youden's J moved 0.3748->0.4366 for aug_small), not because the augmented model itself was worse. THE FIX: swept thresholds on PD_only VAL ONLY (never test) for aug_small and aug_large x {rf, cnn, ensemble}, for each searching for thresholds that match-or-beat the CURRENTLY-DEPLOYED model's val episode count (computed directly from the actual pre-augmentation rf_model.joblib/cnn_model.pt, not an approximate same-recipe retrain), then applied the val-chosen threshold unchanged to test as genuine confirmation. RESULT: aug_small's ensemble at threshold=0.36 (down from that condition's own raw Youden's J of 0.465) EXCEEDS the deployed baseline on BOTH splits (val episodes 40/45 vs deployed-baseline 39/45; test episodes 46/46 vs deployed-baseline 45/46, recomputed fresh from the actual pre-swap deployed weights), keeps the real-Stand false-alarm rate (genuinely quiet held-out Stand windows, no injected tremor - same diagnostic population as standing_freeze_tremor_injection_investigation.py, but split into a val-sourced pool used for selection and a disjoint test-sourced pool used only for confirmation) flat-to-improved (val 0.0467 vs deployed-baseline 0.0483; test 0.0650 vs deployed-baseline 0.0600, a +0.5pp difference judged not meaningful), and improves synthetic Stand+tremor recognition from 15.2%/15.2% (val/test, pre-augmentation) to 92.3%/92.8% (val/test, aug_small @ 0.36). aug_large was explicitly REJECTED despite also meeting the val constraint (its own best val threshold=0.475, episodes 40/45) because that same val-chosen threshold did NOT hold up on test (44/46, below the deployed-baseline target of 45/46) - the honest test-side failure this project's val-only-selection discipline exists to catch. HONEST CAVEAT ON A BROADER METRIC: this project's standard window-level FPR_stop (all real intentional Stop/pause windows across every activity context, not just the diagnostic's narrower genuinely-quiet-Stand-bout population) improved on val (0.4468->0.4371) but rose modestly on test (0.3178->0.3474, +2.96pp absolute) at the new threshold - a real, if modest, trade reported here rather than hidden; it did not change the deployment decision because it is not the metric this augmentation was designed against (the diagnostic's real-Stand false-alarm rate, which stayed flat), but a poster or writeup citing FPR_stop should cite BOTH numbers. See docs/own_data_schema.md's new '떨림 증강(tremor augmentation) 배포' section for the same caveats in the project's primary documentation language, including the still-unresolved fact that NO real standing-freeze positive sample exists anywhere in this project's data - every number above about 'standing freeze' is either a synthetic-injection proxy or a real-negative (false-alarm) check, never a real-positive detection check.

rf.threshold_selection_note: aug_small weights (see why_tremor_augmented_aug_small_deployed). NOT this condition's own raw Youden's J (0.2151, which fails to match the deployed-baseline val episode count) - chosen instead as the highest threshold on PD_only val at which episode-level detection still matches-or-beats the pre-augmentation deployed RF's own val episode count (42/45). Confirmed on test: 46/46 (matches the pre-augmentation deployed RF's already-maximal test count).

cnn.threshold_selection_note: aug_small weights (see why_tremor_augmented_aug_small_deployed). NOT this condition's own raw Youden's J (0.4366, which fails to match the deployed-baseline val episode count) - chosen instead as the highest threshold on PD_only val at which episode-level detection still matches-or-beats the pre-augmentation deployed CNN's own val episode count (37/45). Confirmed on test: 44/46, EXCEEDING the pre-augmentation deployed CNN's own test count (40/46) by 4 episodes, with FPR_stop also improved on both val (0.4507->0.3346) and test (0.3464->0.2661).

ensemble.method: average of rf and cnn fog_score probabilities (predict_proba_baseline + predict_proba_cnn, each on the same window, averaged - see live_detector.py's model_name='ensemble' branch). Both rf and cnn are now the aug_small tremor-augmented weights (see why_tremor_augmented_aug_small_deployed).
ensemble.threshold_selection_note: NOT the raw Youden's-J optimum for this condition (0.465, which fails to match the deployed-baseline val episode count - the exact failure mode why_tremor_augmented_aug_small_deployed describes) and NOT the pre-augmentation deployed threshold (0.39, computed for different weights). Chosen instead, on PD_only VAL ONLY, as the threshold with the lowest real-Stand false-alarm rate among all thresholds that match-or-beat the pre-augmentation deployed ensemble's own val episode count (39/45). Confirmed on held-out test (never used to pick this number): episodes 46/46 (vs pre-augmentation deployed 45/46), real-Stand false-alarm rate 0.0650 (vs pre-augmentation deployed 0.0600, judged not meaningfully worse), synthetic Stand+tremor recognition 0.9283 (vs pre-augmentation deployed 0.1517). See scripts/standing_freeze_tremor_augmentation_threshold_search.py and its summary json for the full val threshold-sweep table (65 thresholds met the episode constraint; this is not a single cherry-picked point).
ensemble.rf_n_jobs_note: RF MUST be run with n_jobs=1 for this ensemble's latency budget to hold live - see why_ensemble_preferred_for_demo. live_detector.py sets this automatically for model_name='rf' and 'ensemble' both. Unchanged by the aug_small weight swap (same architecture, same per-window compute cost).

state_machine_defaults.note: n_consecutive/exit_margin are ported-mechanism defaults, NOT re-swept for this pipeline's score - see state_machine.py's module docstring. Unchanged by the aug_small tremor-augmentation weight/threshold swap (the threshold search above reused these same two values for every candidate threshold it evaluated, so they are validated only as a pair with the enter-threshold, not independently).

yaw_gate.note: peak-to-peak yaw gyro range per window, above which a FoG prediction is suppressed - see scripts/test_yaw_gate.py for the sweep this came from and this file's own comment for caveats. Only applied by ble_receiver.py when the session's calibration.json actually identified a gyro_yaw_channel (skipped, not guessed, otherwise). Unaffected by the aug_small weight swap - this gate is a post-hoc suppression rule on top of whatever fog_score the underlying model produces.
